'''Anahila Lose Kanongata'a''' (born 1969) is a New Zealand social worker and politician. She served as a [[New Zealand House of Representatives|Member of Parliament]] for the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] from 2017 to 2023.

==Early life and career==
Kanongata'a was born in [[Tonga]]. When she was a child, her single mother went to work in New Zealand, leaving her children in the custody of her father. When her mother and stepfather became permanent residents, she came to New Zealand in 1980 and settled in a state house in [[Onehunga]].<ref name="backbencher2">{{cite web |date=2 January 2018 |title=Meet the backbencher: Anahila Kanongata'a-Suisuiki |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11964608 |access-date=5 January 2018 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref> At the time, she did not speak English.<ref name="backbencher2" /> She left school in the sixth form and began working as a bank teller.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Newhsub Nation Backstory: Labour MP Anahila Kanongata'a recounts mother's funeral under Covid restrictions |language=en |work=[[Newshub]] |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/shows/2023/05/newhsub-nation-backstory-labour-mp-anahila-kanongata-a-recounts-mother-s-funeral-under-covid-restrictions.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102164424/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/shows/2023/05/newhsub-nation-backstory-labour-mp-anahila-kanongata-a-recounts-mother-s-funeral-under-covid-restrictions.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 January 2024 |access-date=2024-01-01}}</ref> She married her first husband and had two children before she turned 20.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Hopgood |first=Sela Jane |date=2022-02-09 |title=This social media-friendly Pasifika MP is doing it for her community |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/09-02-2022/this-social-media-friendly-pasifika-mp-is-doing-it-for-her-community |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=The Spinoff |language=en}}</ref>

Aged 30, Kanongata'a won a scholarship to study either economics or social work at the University of Auckland. She chose social work and worked as a social worker and manager for the [[Ministry of Social Development (New Zealand)|Ministry of Social Development]] and [[Oranga Tamariki]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Fuatai |first=Teuila |date=2018-03-06 |title=From Tonga to NZ's Parliament |url=http://newsroom.co.nz/2018/03/06/thesuper-sub-mp-anahila-kanongataa-suisuiki/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=Newsroom |language=en-US}}</ref> She was on the national executive of [[P.A.C.I.F.I.C.A]] Incorporated.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Executive |url=http://www.pacifica.org.nz/?page_id=21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408001353/http://www.pacifica.org.nz/?page_id=21 |archive-date=8 April 2017 |access-date=1 January 2024 |publisher=P.A.C.I.F.I.C.A Inc.}}</ref>

She became a [[justice of the peace]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Justices of the Peace Appointed - 2013-go2578 - New Zealand Gazette |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2013-go2578 |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=gazette.govt.nz}}</ref>

== Early political career ==
Kanongata'a made three attempts at a political career in the early 2010s. In 2010, under her married name Anahila Suisuiki, she contested a position on the [[Manurewa Local Board]] as an independent, finishing last among 16 candidates.<ref name=":2" /> Following this run, she joined the Labour Party and ran unsuccessfully as a list-only candidate at both the {{NZ election link|2011}} (ranked 51) and {{NZ election link|2014}} (ranked 49).<ref>{{cite press release |title=Labour Party List 2011 |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1104/S00194/labour-party-list-2011.htm |publisher=[[New Zealand Labour Party]] |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=10 April 2011 |access-date=10 April 2011}}</ref><ref name="labour-list2">{{cite press release |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1406/S00372/labour-list-for-the-2014-election-announced.htm |title=Labour List for the 2014 Election Announced |publisher=[[New Zealand Labour Party]] |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=23 June 2014 |access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> She unsuccessfully contested the Labour Party candidate selection for [[Manukau East]] in 2014, losing to [[Jenny Salesa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberts |first=Sarah |date=27 February 2014 |title=Labour picks Manukau East candidate |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/manukau-courier/9771379/Labour-picks-Manukau-East-candidate |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=www.stuff.co.nz}}</ref>

She held internal Labour party offices, including as the vice chair of Labour's women's council and as chair of the Manurewa electorate committee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anahila Lose Kanonga'ata-Suisuiki CV |url=https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/1402/Anahila_KanongataaSuisuiki.pdf |access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref>

===First term, 2017–2020===
Kanongata'a stood as a list only candidate for Labour at the {{NZ election link|2017}} (ranked 37)<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 August 2017 |title=Revised Labour Party List for the 2017 Election |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1708/S00314/revised-labour-party-list-for-the-2017-election.htm |access-date=2 September 2017 |publisher=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]]}}</ref> and was elected as a list MP through Labour's party vote result of 36.9%.

In her first term, she served on the health committee (2017–2018) and the social services committee (2018–2020).<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Kanongata'a, Anahila - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/kanongataa-anahila/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> She was appointed to the Abortion Legislation Committee, which considered the [[Abortion Legislation Act 2020|Abortion Legislation Bill]] that proposed eliminating most legal restrictions on abortion in New Zealand, in 2019.<ref name="Stuff 8 October 20192">{{cite news |last1=Rosenberg |first1=Matthew |date=8 October 2019 |title=Abortion bill: Emotions run high at select committee hearing in Auckland |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/116396137/abortion-bill-emotions-run-high-at-select-committee-hearing-in-auckland |accessdate=9 October 2019}}</ref> She opposed the bill during all three readings of the bill in Parliament, which subsequently passed into law in March 2020.<ref name=":4">{{cite news |last1=Walls |first1=Jason |date=8 August 2019 |title=How Members of Parliament voted in the first reading of the Abortion Legislation Bill |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12256951 |accessdate=9 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{cite news |last1=Cheng |first1=Derek |date=3 March 2020 |title=Abortion law reform passes next parliamentary hurdle comfortably |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12313615 |url-status=live |accessdate=3 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605133914/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12313615 |archive-date=5 June 2020}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{cite web |last= |first= |date=18 March 2020 |title=Abortion Legislation Bill — Third Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20200318_20200318_24 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720222000/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20200318_20200318_24 |archive-date=20 July 2020 |accessdate=18 March 2020 |website= |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]}}</ref>

In March 2018, a [[private member's bill]] in Kanongata'a's name was drawn from the member's ballot and subsequently was introduced to Parliament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Members' bill ballot for Thursday, 22 March 2018 - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/members-bills-ballots-archive/members-bill-ballot-for-thursday-22-march-2018/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> The Oaths and Declarations (Members of Parliament) Amendment Bill sought to enable members of Parliament to make their [[Oath of Allegiance (New Zealand)|oaths of allegiance]] in a language other than English or te reo Māori, which are the two allowed languages under the Oaths and Declarations Act 1957.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Oaths and Declarations (Members of Parliament) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/1a24ff85-2642-4107-9b71-07667bc76fcb?Tab=history |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=bills.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> Members may make an unofficial oath in another language with the consent of the House, but must make one in an official language. The bill failed at its first reading 54–65.<ref name=":7" />

===Second term, 2020–2023===
In the [[2020 New Zealand general election]], Kanongata'a contested the [[Papakura (New Zealand electorate)|Papakura]] electorate, challenging [[Judith Collins]], the [[Leader of the Opposition (New Zealand)|Leader of the Opposition]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Forbes |first1=Steve |date=27 July 2020 |title=Election 2020: Labour backbencher's David and Goliath battle with 'Crusher' Collins |language=en-NZ |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12351399}}</ref> Kanongata'a-Suisuiki lost to Collins by a final margin of 5,583 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Papakura – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-38.html |access-date=12 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref> However, she returned to Parliament on the Labour Party list.<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html |access-date=12 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref> In her second term, she served on the environment committee and the social services committee.<ref name=":3" />

A second member's bill in Kanongata'a's name was drawn in June 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Members' bill ballot for Thursday, 18 June 2020 - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/members-bills-ballots-archive/members-bill-ballot-for-thursday-18-june-2020/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> The District Court (Protection of Judgment Debtors with Disabilities) Amendment Bill proposed a prohibition on the seizure of items from [[judgment debtor]]s with disabilities if those items are necessary for their care, support or independence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=District Court (Protection of Judgment Debtors with Disabilities) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/caecd80b-e623-40df-b9cd-50fbe04a5677?Tab=history |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=bills.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> The bill passed its third reading unanimously on 30 June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=District Court (Protection of Judgment Debtors with Disabilities) Amendment Bill — Third Reading - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20210630_20210630_16 |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> Another judgment debtors bill in Kanongata'a's name was drawn on 27 July 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members' bills ballot for Thursday, 27 July 2023 |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/2/65fa58c3-50f8-420e-dc15-08db8e23afc4 |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=bills.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> The District Court (Protecting Judgment Debtors on Main Benefit) Amendment Bill did not complete its first reading before the House rose for the 2023 general election, in which Kanonga'ata was not re-elected; it was subsequently transferred to [[Duncan Webb]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=District Court (Protecting Judgment Debtors on Main Benefit) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/547f9c48-c536-4d7d-e6f9-08db8e47efec?Tab=hansard |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=bills.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref>

In March 2021, Kanongata'a voted against the proposed [[Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion (Safe Areas) Amendment Act 2022]], claiming that the creation of safe areas around abortion providers amounted to the "erosion of freedom of expression".<ref name=":8">{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |date=12 March 2021 |title=How MPs voted on law change that would allow safe zones around abortion clinics |work=[[Newshub]] |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/03/how-mps-voted-on-law-change-that-would-allow-safe-zones-around-abortion-clinics.html |url-status=dead |access-date=30 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316122718/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/03/how-mps-voted-on-law-change-that-would-allow-safe-zones-around-abortion-clinics.html |archive-date=16 March 2021}}</ref> She also voted against the bill during its second and third readings in 2022.<ref name=":9">{{cite web |date=16 February 2022 |title=Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion (Safe Areas) Amendment Bill — Second Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20220215_20220216_28 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220301063103/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20220215_20220216_28 |archive-date=1 March 2022 |access-date=1 March 2022 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{cite web |date=16 March 2022 |title=Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion (Safe Areas) Amendment Bill — Third Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20220316_20220316_36 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220317001313/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20220316_20220316_36 |archive-date=17 March 2022 |access-date=26 April 2022 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]}}</ref>

In January 2022, with colleague [[Jenny Salesa]], Kanonga'ata set up the Aotearoa Tonga Relief Committee to support the response to the [[2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooke |first=Henry |date=2022-01-18 |title=Tonga eruption: The island can rebuild but needs NZ's help, MPs say |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300498205/tonga-eruption-the-island-can-rebuild-but-needs-nzs-help-mps-say |access-date=2024-01-02 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref>

During the [[2023 New Zealand general election]], Kanonga'ata contested the Papakura electorate a second time but failed to unseat National MP Judith Collins, who won by a margin of 13,519 votes.<ref>{{cite web |date=3 November 2023 |title=Papakura - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-38.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123104123/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-38.html |archive-date=23 November 2023 |access-date=10 December 2023 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref> Ranked 34 on the Labour Party list, she was not returned to Parliament due to Labour's poorer result than at the previous election.<ref>{{cite web |date=15 October 2023 |title=Election 2023: Defeated Labour MPs speak out after devastating loss |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/10/election-2023-defeated-labour-mps-speak-out-after-devastating-loss.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017081459/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/10/election-2023-defeated-labour-mps-speak-out-after-devastating-loss.html |archive-date=17 October 2023 |access-date=10 December 2023 |publisher=[[Newshub]]}}</ref>

== Personal views ==
Kanonga'ata was a member of the social conservative wing of the Labour Party. She consistently voted against progressive legislation including the [[End of Life Choice Act 2019|End of Life Choice Bill]],<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |date=2019-11-13 |title=The End of Life Choice Debate: in pictures |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/the-house/audio/2018722102/the-end-of-life-choice-debate-in-pictures-and-the-words-of-mps |access-date=2024-01-02 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref> the [[Abortion Legislation Act 2020|Abortion Legislation Bill]],<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> and the [[Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion (Safe Areas) Amendment Act 2022|Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion (Safe Areas) Amendment Bill]].<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /> In some speeches, she attributed her views to her Christian faith.<ref name=":11" />
